imagegen_provenance.exact_prompt:
Make ONE targeted edit of Reference 1 to correct its lower-body gait pose into a compact canonical K3 right-leg passing drawing. Reference 1 is the editable base and absolute authority for the rabbit's exact identity, head, both ears, torso, overalls, shirt, tool pouch, palette, outline, shading, canvas, camera and overall scale. Preserve all pixels and proportions above the hips as closely as possible. Preserve the same full-body size, no zoom/crop, and same head-to-torso ratio. This is a small limb-pose adjustment, not a character redesign.

Reference 2 is the accepted K5 right-contact pose, used only for character design consistency, fixed head/torso scale and limb anatomy; do not copy its contact pose. Reference 3 is original K2, used only as neighboring phase and support-foot baseline cue.

Draw exactly one full-body rabbit-worker facing directly away from camera, walking north, centered on the same square transparent canvas and at the same scale as Reference 1. Canonical K3 is the compact passing moment AFTER left weight-down (K2) and BEFORE right knee-up (Reference 1's current leg pose, retained as K4 candidate). Keep the anatomical LEFT leg on screen-left as the weight-bearing support leg; its boot stays fully flat and planted on the same baseline as Reference 3. Move only the anatomical RIGHT leg on screen-right forward beneath the pelvis so its ankle passes close to the centerline under the right hip. Raise the right boot only a small amount above the ground, with the toe distinctly pointed down and the heel lifted slightly; show the boot from rear/side with no broad sole facing camera. The right knee is only slightly bent and stays low, not lifted high. The right thigh, shin, ankle and boot remain anatomically continuous and clearly connected to the screen-right pelvis. Do not cross legs, swap owners, hide the right leg, or create a second raised foot.

Make only the natural compact counter-swing: anatomical LEFT arm on screen-left trails slightly back; anatomical RIGHT arm on screen-right moves slightly forward, relaxed, without obstructing the right hip pouch. Keep the torso and head facing straight away, level and motion-stable. Maintain exact proportions: do not enlarge head, ears, torso, sleeves, tail, pouch, boots, or character; do not shorten legs or make body squat. Keep exactly two long orange rabbit ears, two arms, two hands, two legs, two boots, one fluffy white tail, white sleeves, white shirt, blue denim overalls, brass strap buttons, brown belt, and one brown pouch on the rabbit's anatomical right hip (screen-right) with exactly one red handled tool and one yellow handled tool. Preserve the art style, texture, colors and outline from Reference 1. No extra appendages/tools, no duplicate character, no mirror, no ground shadow or matte. Pixels outside the character must be transparent.
